name: Mast v0.9.0
body:
Mast 0.9.0 gives the dev servers a project runs on your machine their own trusted `https://….test` address beside the API's. It also lets you run and stop saved commands from anywhere, and the app sees what you started.

- **HTTPS for host commands.** A frontend in its own repo, run as one of the API project's commands (`vp dev` with `cwd: ../suite`), can have its own domain on the same local HTTPS proxy. Open **HTTPS** on the project card:
  - One dialog lists the app and every command that runs on this machine.
  - It suggests sibling names, such as `api.thinksolar.test` and `suite.thinksolar.test`.
  - It warns while a command would be on a different site from the app, and offers to move one of them.
- **The address follows the dev server.** Mast reads the port from the command's own output: Vite's `Local:` line, webpack's, artisan's `Server running on` and others. A Vite that moves to 5174 keeps its address. You can also pin a port. Until a port is known, the domain explains what it's waiting for instead of failing silently.
- **Enabling a domain checks it end to end.** One request goes through the proxy, and the operation names what's in the way:
  - nothing listening on the port;
  - Vite refusing the host name (`server.allowedHosts`);
  - a Laravel `.env` whose `SESSION_DOMAIN` or `SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS` keeps a Sanctum session from crossing between frontend and API.

  This now applies to the app's own domain too.
- **The proxy reaches localhost-only servers.** On a native Linux Docker engine, the proxy now runs on the host network, so a dev server listening only on `127.0.0.1` is reachable. Docker Desktop, OrbStack, colima, rootless Docker, macOS and Windows keep the bridged proxy. An existing proxy moves over the next time a domain is enabled, keeping its certificates. Caddy's admin API moves from a TCP port to a socket.
- **Commands are tracked by the engine.** A saved command started from the CLI, a bar widget or another window now shows as running in the app. You can stop or restart it from there, and it isn't auto-started a second time. Starting a command that's already running is refused, whoever asks.
- **CLI:**
  ```
  mast start <project> --command dev     # runs in the app's engine and keeps running
  mast stop <project> --command dev      # whoever started it
  mast workspace start <workspace>       # members in dependency order
  mast workspace stop <workspace>
  mast agents <project> --stop <pid>     # one process the agents report lists
  mast agents --clean-up [--dry-run]     # what the app's Clean up ticks by itself
  ```
  A saved command needs the desktop app or `mast-daemon` running, so that it outlives the CLI.
- **`mast://agents`** opens the Agents page.
- **MCP** project details list each command's local domain. MCP stays read-only for starting and stopping.

The CLI and the desktop app must be on the same minor version: update both to 0.9.

Desktop installers and CLI/daemon archives are provided for Linux x86_64/ARM64, macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, and Windows x86_64.

Changes: [local HTTPS for host commands #62](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/62), [engine-tracked commands and CLI verbs #63](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/63).

name: Mast v0.8.0
body:
Mast 0.8.0 shows what coding agents are doing in your projects — the sessions working now, the git worktrees they make, and everything they start and leave running — and lets you clean it up.

- **Agents page.** Everything agents are doing across your projects in one place:
  - Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Aider, opencode, Cursor's agent and other sessions working right now, in the checkout or a worktree, with what each is running.
  - Dev servers, workers, `sail`/`docker` clients and headless browsers left running after their session ended, with the memory they hold.
  - Process trees in the app container that Mast didn't start.
  - Worktrees, found wherever they live: `.claude/worktrees/`, Codex's and Cursor's folders, or anywhere `git worktree add` put them. Each shows its branch, uncommitted changes, commits the checkout doesn't have, and any containers started from it.
  - The sidebar item pulses while an agent is working and turns amber with a count of what's left running unused.
- **On each project's card.** The same section appears on the project it belongs to, so leftovers show up where you're already looking.
- **Clean up.** One list of every leftover, with what nothing is using already ticked. Review it once and clear it all. Things a live agent started stay unticked, and worktrees are never removed from it.
- **Worktree actions.**
  - Stop or remove a worktree's containers; named volumes are kept.
  - Forget worktrees whose directory is gone.
  - Remove a worktree. Mast stops what runs in it and removes its containers first, and keeps the branch. It refuses while an agent is still working there, and asks separately before discarding uncommitted changes.
- **For agents.** `mast agents` on the CLI and a read-only `mast_agents` MCP tool show the same picture. The MCP server now asks agents to check it before starting a dev server or `sail up`, and again before finishing.
- **Fixes:**
  - A worktree inside the project folder could have its app container read as the project's own. Worktree containers are now kept apart.
  - A worktree whose copied `.env` shares the project's compose name gets a warning, because `sail up` there replaces the project's containers.
  - Mast's own `git status` no longer takes the index lock, so it can't make an agent's `git commit` fail.

Processes on the host are watched on Linux. macOS and Windows show worktrees, their containers and what runs in app containers.

The CLI and the desktop app must be on the same minor version: update both to 0.8.

Desktop installers and CLI/daemon archives are provided for Linux x86_64/ARM64, macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, and Windows x86_64.

Changes: [agents and worktrees #61](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/61).

name: Mast v0.7.5
body:
Mast 0.7.5 shows what is running in a project's app container, makes Stop work for Sail commands, and fixes the titlebar on KDE Plasma under Wayland.

- Stop works for Sail commands. Since 0.7.2, stopping a command that runs through Sail, such as `sail artisan dev` or `sail npm run dev`, reported success and stopped nothing. The next Start, Restart or auto-start then launched a second copy beside the first: two Horizon masters, two schedulers running every task twice, and a Vite whose exit deleted `public/hot`, so pages served an old build. Mast now records each run inside the container, and stops it and everything beneath it as the user that started it.
- "In the app container" on the project card. Every process tree running in the app container gets a chip showing who started it, the memory it holds and how long it has run. Green is a command Mast is running. Amber is anything else: a copy an earlier Mast session left, something started from a terminal or by an agent, or an orphan. The chip's menu shows the command line and the daemons inside, and offers Stop for anything Mast isn't running. Copies left by 0.7.4 and earlier appear here as started outside Mast.
- Duplicates are flagged. Horizon, the scheduler, Reverb, Vite or Pail running more than once gets an advisory that explains the cost and offers to stop each copy Mast isn't running. Before a Sail command runs, any copy of that same command an earlier Mast session left running is stopped, and the output says so. Nothing started outside Mast is stopped without a click.
- Process chips show what is actually running. A daemon counts as running only when a process is that daemon, so a Horizon that has died inside a still-running `artisan dev` no longer shows green.
- Vite and `public/hot`. Advisories cover Vite running without its hot file, a hot file pointing at a different dev server, and a hot file pointing where nothing listens. Each offers Restart for the dev command or Remove `public/hot`.
- Stopping a command no longer hangs on a leftover process. A descendant that survives SIGTERM is killed when the grace period ends, and a background process a command leaves running no longer keeps the command open.
- KDE Plasma on Wayland: the titlebar's minimise, maximise and close buttons now work, and KWin draws the titlebar at its normal height. Tauri is updated to 2.12.3. Tiling desktops such as Hyprland still have no titlebar.

Desktop installers and CLI/daemon archives are provided for Linux x86_64/ARM64, macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, and Windows x86_64.

Changes: [KDE Wayland titlebar #54](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/54), [Stop for Sail commands #55](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/55), [app container processes #56](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/56), [stopping commands with leftover descendants #58](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/58).

name: Mast v0.7.4
body:
Mast 0.7.4 makes Laravel Reverb work on a project's local HTTPS address.

- Reverb's WebSocket reaches `wss://myapp.test`. An HTTPS page can only open a secure socket, so Echo connects through the local proxy, which used to forward everything to the app's port. For a project running Reverb, the proxy now sends WebSocket upgrades on `/app/*` to the port the app container publishes for Reverb. Ordinary `/app/…` pages still reach the app.
- Sail doesn't publish Reverb's port by default. Enabling a domain on a project that runs Reverb without that mapping now says so and shows the ports entry to add.
- The proxy follows port changes. A moved `APP_PORT`, or a Reverb port published after the domain was enabled, reaches the proxy on the next refresh instead of waiting for the domain to be toggled. Hand edits to the generated Caddyfile no longer survive that refresh.

Desktop installers and CLI/daemon archives are provided for Linux x86_64/ARM64, macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, and Windows x86_64.

Changes: [Reverb over local HTTPS #52](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/52).

name: Mast v0.7.3
body:
Mast 0.7.3 makes the CLI a reliable status source for scripts and desktop widgets, fixes two engine-ownership problems, and repairs Close to tray.

- `mast status --json` prints the engine snapshot as one document — the same shape the desktop app reads — for scripts and desktop widgets such as the Omarchy bar plugin.
- `mast status` waits for every project's compose pass before answering. An embedded engine could previously report `0/0 services`, drop branches, or show a running project as stopped when asked too early.
- Reading verbs (`status`, `diagnose`, `history`, `snapshots`) no longer take the engine's mutation lock. A widget polling status every thirty seconds held it for two seconds each time, and a desktop app launched in that window stayed read-only for its whole run.
- The desktop app keeps asking for ownership instead of staying read-only, serves the shared socket once it has it, and clears the read-only badge.
- App → Close to tray works. The webview's close request was refused for lack of the `core:window:allow-close` permission, silently, on every platform; the window manager's close request had always hidden the window correctly.
- Omarchy: the README documents the AppImage as the build to use and how to add the Mast bar widget.

Desktop installers and CLI/daemon archives are provided for Linux x86_64/ARM64, macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, and Windows x86_64.

Changes: [status --json, lock-free reads, ownership retry, Close to tray #51](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/51).

name: Mast v0.7.2
body:
Mast 0.7.2 fixes project cleanup, process restarts, and activity indicators.

- Removing a watched directory removes its projects from Mast unless another directory still covers them, stops managed commands, and cleans up workspace references. Project files stay on disk.
- Moved or missing project folders show a clear path error and recover when restored.
- Queue workers, Horizon, the scheduler, and Reverb started through Mast restart after application code or configuration changes.
- Saved commands now have Restart. Managed Sail commands stop their container processes before restarting, and failed cleanup must succeed before a retry can launch another process.
- Windows command cancellation and timeouts now terminate the owned process tree instead of waiting indefinitely.
- Running Laravel daemons no longer leave the project spinner active or lock project controls. Starting, stopping, cancellation, and failure indicators now update consistently.
- Removed projects no longer leave stale selections, logs, or pending auto-starts behind. Connection failures expose Reconnect, and synchronization handles interrupted snapshot streams.

Desktop installers and CLI/daemon archives are provided for Linux x86_64/ARM64, macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, and Windows x86_64.

Validation: [Linux, macOS, and Windows CI](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/actions/runs/35304655796) passed, alongside 192 frontend tests and production builds. Windows desktop runtime tests remain excluded on hosted runners; the desktop crate is compiled.

Changes: [lifecycle and restart fixes #49](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/49), [macOS test-fixture fix #50](https://github.com/stackrats/mast/pull/50).

name: Mast 0.7.1
body:
Mast now runs on Arch Linux and Hyprland. Tested on Omarchy.

## Linux packaging

- **The AppImage starts on any Mesa.** It bundled four `libwayland-*` files from the build machine, and on any host whose Mesa differed from Ubuntu's the app aborted with `EGL_BAD_PARAMETER` before drawing a window. They are no longer bundled. Everything else — WebKit, GTK, ICU — is unaffected.
- **The AppImage runs as native Wayland.** Its launcher forced `GDK_BACKEND=x11`, putting the app on XWayland under every Wayland desktop to dodge a Tauri 1.5 crash that no longer applies. It now prefers Wayland, falls back to X11, and respects a `GDK_BACKEND` you export yourself.

## Tiling window managers

- The sidebar and logs panel re-clamp against the live window size, so a tile that shrinks the window no longer crushes the content pane — and the widths you dragged come back when it grows.
- Below 520px the sidebar floats over the content instead of taking space from it. `Ctrl B` toggles it.
- Menus stay inside the window instead of forcing a horizontal scrollbar.
- **Interface size** is a slider in Settings (50–200%), with `Ctrl +` / `Ctrl -` / `Ctrl 0`. A tiling session starts at 75%.
- No titlebar on tiling desktops; the window manager's border is what you see.
- The wordmark is drawn as vectors, in the menubar and the splash, so it renders at every size and zoom.

## Docker

When Docker cannot be reached, the card says which of four things is wrong — not installed, not running, permission denied, unreachable — and names the fix, with the command as code. The raw error is one click away rather than the headline.

## Fixes

- Project card header wraps in narrow windows instead of breaking the path character by character.
- Splash tagline is one line wherever one line fits.

Arch users: the `.deb` and `.rpm` are not for you — use `Mast_0.7.1_amd64.AppImage`. Docker needs to be installed and running, and your user in the `docker` group.

name: Mast v0.7.0
body:
The team release: your project setup now travels with the repo, your workers stay alive, your data has a way back, and getting a teammate running is one link.

## mast.yml — commands that travel with the repo

Saved commands can now live in a `mast.yml` committed at the project root. Clone, import, done — everyone gets the same commands, start ordering, and readiness checks. Saving a command under the same name overrides the shared one locally, mistakes in the file become named warnings (never a project that refuses to load), and the **Share** chip writes your current saved commands into a first `mast.yml` for you.

## Commands that stay alive

- **Auto-restart**: any exit you didn't ask for relaunches the command with backoff; a crash loop stops after five rapid exits instead of hammering the same failure.
- **Restart on change**: give a command globs like `app/** config/**` and it's stopped and relaunched when matching files change — what a queue worker needs to ever see new code.

## Data snapshots

Any service with named volumes gets **Data snapshots** on its chip: one click copies its volumes (container briefly stopped for a clean copy, restarted after) into labeled docker volumes on your machine. Restore is deliberately harder than take — a two-step confirm that offers to snapshot the current data first, checked by default. Snapshots survive reinstalls, show up in `docker volume ls`, and delete like anything else. Also from the CLI (`mast snapshot`, `mast snapshots`) and MCP — restore stays in the app, behind its confirm.

## Clone the team's project

The add-project dialog gained a **From Git** mode: it clones, bootstraps exactly what a fresh clone is missing (containerized `composer install`, `.env` from `.env.example`, an app key), and imports — `mast.yml` commands included. URLs with embedded credentials are refused: effect history records every command verbatim, and a token must never land there.

## Open in Mast — mast:// links

Put `mast://clone?url=…` in your repo's README and onboarding becomes one click: Mast opens with the dialog prefilled. `mast://project/<name>` jumps to an existing project. Links can only navigate or prefill — never clone, start, or stop anything by themselves — because any webpage can fire a registered URL scheme. You still click the button.

**Behavior change**: launching Mast while it's already running now surfaces the existing window instead of opening a second read-only one. The CLI keeps its read-only fallback.

## Mast speaks MCP

`mast mcp` runs a Model Context Protocol server over stdio against the same engine as the app — register it in your coding agent's MCP settings and the agent gets status, container logs, the parsed Laravel log with stack traces, log captures, diagnostics, history, wait-for-healthy, the lifecycle verbs, saved-command execution (saved commands only — your curated list is the consent boundary), and snapshot take/list.

## Quality of life

- Amber **attention dots** on sidebar and fleet rows for things that happened while you weren't looking; visiting the project clears them.
- Sidebar: type-to-filter, collapsible workspaces and sections, right-click menus on projects *and* workspaces, `Ctrl`+`1`–`9` project jumps.
- Stack-trace file paths in the Laravel log and captures are **clickable** — your editor opens at the line.
- A **Tinker** button on the project card, and **Open in database client** next to connection info.
- Status dots carry their meaning in a tooltip, not just a color.

## Upgrading

The wire format grew this release: update the desktop app and the CLI together — a 0.6 CLI and a 0.7 app will refuse to share the daemon socket, and the error tells you which one is behind.

**macOS and Windows note**: the `mast://` scheme registration on these platforms ships here for the first time — if a link doesn't open the app, that's exactly the report we want.

name: Mast v0.6.0
body:
## The fleet, a command palette, and compose measured against Sail's own stubs

Six features aimed at the friction that only shows up once Sail is part of your daily work rather than something you just installed.

### One screen for every project

Running ten Sail projects means thirty-odd containers, and the machine gets warm. Mast already measured what each project cost; it just never showed them together. **Home now carries a fleet table** — containers, cores and memory per project, dearest at the top — and offers to stop the ones that have gone quiet.

*Quiet* is deliberately not *idle*. All Mast can honestly say is that a project has stayed under a CPU threshold for the length of the sample window, so that is what the badge and the tooltip say. The verdict needs a full window of evidence, and it is judged on every sample rather than an average — a project that spiked once and settled is being used.

### Ctrl-K reaches everything

Mast had no keyboard handling at all. **`Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`K` now opens a command palette** over every project, lifecycle verb, external-tool launch, saved command, workspace and dialog, with fuzzy matching that ranks a title hit above a keyword one. Commands that cannot work are not offered — a stopped project has no Stop. Discoverable from the App menu, which shows the accelerator.

### PHP extensions install themselves

Sail added a `PHP_EXTENSIONS` build arg in June ([laravel/sail#879](https://github.com/laravel/sail/pull/879)), which removed the reason this was parked: installing an extension no longer means hand-editing a vendored Dockerfile. **Pick extensions in the PHP runtime dialog** and Mast rewrites the build arg, rebuilds without cache, recreates the container and verifies it.

Two refusals matter more than the happy path. Extension names are checked against the apt package alphabet, because the runtime expands the list unquoted. And a runtime published before #879 is refused outright with an explanation — Docker only *warns* about a build arg the Dockerfile never declares, so the edit would otherwise rebuild for minutes and install precisely nothing.

### Your compose file, against the stubs your Sail would write today

A compose file is generated once at install and is yours from then on, so when upstream fixes a stub, projects created earlier keep the broken version and nothing says so. Recent examples: a second MongoDB volume without which the container can fail to restart ([#883](https://github.com/laravel/sail/pull/883)), and RabbitMQ env keys the image ignored ([#874](https://github.com/laravel/sail/pull/874)).

**Mast now compares each service against `vendor/laravel/sail/stubs`** — what your installed Sail would generate today — and reports what the stub has that your file does not. It notices the next such fix without anyone adding a rule.

This is a two-way compare, not a three-way one, and it says so. Nothing records the stub a file was generated from, so a difference cannot be attributed to a side; the finding is informational, because what looks like a gap can equally be something you removed on purpose. Local additions and deliberate pins stay silent, and list order is never treated as drift.

### Slow project files, named as the host problem they are

Bind-mount latency is the most-cited complaint about Sail and is entirely a property of the host: on Linux a bind mount *is* the filesystem, but elsewhere every file crosses a VM boundary — and a Laravel tree is the worst shape for that.

Mast **identifies your container runtime and gives advice specific to it**: VirtioFS and where to select it for Docker Desktop, `--mount-type virtiofs` for colima, its own preference for Rancher Desktop, and silence for OrbStack, which already runs near native. Every case also names the mitigation that works regardless — keeping `vendor` and `node_modules` out of the mount as named volumes.

It is not a benchmark. Timing a real write means running a container on every diagnostics pass, and a routine check should not cost that.

### No release ships from a red tree

The release workflow now refuses to build unless CI concluded `success` for the exact commit being released, waiting out a run still in flight. There is no bypass: re-cutting an existing release has to be green too.

---

### Also

- Two flaky tests fixed — an idle-budget test with too little margin on loaded CI runners, and an assertion matching bare port numbers that collided with a nanosecond timestamp in a container name.
- Fleet rows are clickable across their whole width, and stopped projects are no longer listed there — every column is a cost, and a stopped project has none.

### Notes

- macOS and Windows binaries are unsigned.
- The quiet threshold is calibrated from observed readings on a real fleet rather than a measured idle floor. If it flags something you are actually using, it is one constant in `lib/usage.ts`.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/stackrats/mast/compare/v0.5.1...v0.6.0

name: Mast v0.5.1
body:
Rebuilds that outlive the clock, a pnpm repair, ordered commands, and a UI that says what it is doing.

## Fixed

- **Long rebuilds are no longer killed mid-build.** Streamed docker/sail commands are now judged on progress instead of a fixed wall clock: output keeps a command alive, ten minutes of silence ends it, and a two-hour ceiling backstops everything. A killed command reports *stalled* (went quiet) or *timed out* (overran) as two different diagnoses. A cold Sail runtime build — 15+ minutes of apt — previously died at the old 900s limit with the finish line in sight.
- **Node installs Mast runs no longer stall on a question nothing can answer.** They run with `CI=true`, and the lockfile decision is stated explicitly so the CI default cannot flip it.

## pnpm across the container boundary

pnpm records its package store's absolute path at install time and verifies it before every `pnpm run` — a check that can never pass on the other side of a Sail bind mount, even though the installed files work on both sides. The visible symptom: `artisan dev`'s vite lane dying in a NO_TTY retry loop while the site keeps serving.

- Diagnostics now catches this **before it first fires**, reading the recorded store out of `node_modules/.modules.yaml`.
- The failure line itself is classified and explained, with the same one-click repair.
- The repair appends `verifyDepsBeforeRun: false` to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — previewed as a diff, created if missing, a no-op once set. Nothing is reinstalled and nothing else changes.
- A new signature also explains the "failed to set up container networking: network … not found" start failure (a container pinned to a network id that no longer exists).

## Commands

- **Edit in place** — name, command line, working directory, auto-start — and the chip's menu now opens with the literal line it will run.
- **Ordering**: a command can start `after` another, and a command can declare how anything waiting on it knows it is up (`ready when` — the first output line containing the text, matched with its colours stripped). Auto-start waits for the dependency to come up: its ready line, a clean exit, or its output settling. Self-waits, dangling names and cycles are refused at save time with the reason.

## UI

- A busy project shows a spinner and the running verb — in the sidebar and on the card's status badge — instead of the stale status it is leaving. The card adds an elapsed readout and the operation's live last line, so a twenty-minute build is distinguishable from a hang without opening the panel.
- Controls that would change a project are locked while an operation runs on it.
- Streamed output renders its ANSI colours everywhere (Output, History, Captures, service logs) instead of showing escape bytes as punctuation.
- Operations that outlast a minute notify on success, not just failure.

Wire-compatible with a live 0.5.0 daemon (the handshake compares major.minor; the new contract fields are serde-defaulted).

name: Mast v0.5.0
body:
Mast now has a website and a one-line installer, builds for ARM Linux, and refuses to run a mismatched CLI/desktop pair instead of failing obscurely.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://mast.sh/install | sh
```

```powershell
irm https://mast.sh/install.ps1 | iex
```

Both install the `mast` CLI and the headless `mast-daemon` per-user, without `sudo` or elevation. The desktop app remains a separate download from the assets below.

If the desktop app is already installed, the installer **matches its version** rather than taking the newest release — see the handshake note below for why that is now the right default.

## The daemon socket checks builds, not just the protocol

The CLI and the desktop app share a per-user socket so both drive one engine. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is frozen at 1 and deliberately does not move when a DTO grows under the additive rules, so two builds from different minors would both announce protocol 1, agree to talk, and then die inside `serde_json::from_value` on a missing field — a message that says nothing about the real problem.

The handshake now carries the build version as well, compared on major.minor. Both ends check it, and the CLI stops with a clear message rather than silently falling back to an embedded engine that would come up read-only behind the running app.

Builds agreeing on major and minor are compatible; patch releases never move the wire format. Because a peer that announces no version at all is now refused, **a 0.4.x CLI will not pair with a 0.5.0 desktop** — update both.

## Platforms

Prebuilt CLI binaries now cover `linux-x86_64`, **`linux-aarch64`** (new), `macos-aarch64`, `macos-x86_64` and `windows-x86_64`. ARM Linux desktop bundles (deb/rpm/AppImage) ship for the first time in this release, built on a native arm64 runner.

## Also in this release

- The app service leads every project's service list instead of sinking alphabetically
- Project creation installs exactly the services picked — `--with none` when that is none, rather than Sail's four-service default — and the wizard says when that means the project keeps Laravel's SQLite
- The desktop dev command runs the filtered UI workspace, matching its build command

## Notes

- macOS and Windows binaries are unsigned; Gatekeeper and SmartScreen will warn on first launch.
- Releases do not yet publish a `SHA256SUMS` asset, so both installers report that they are skipping checksum verification. Verification is already wired in and begins working as soon as that asset exists.

name: Mast v0.4.0
body:
The cross-platform release.

v0.3.0's assets were rebuilt in place eighteen times as field-testing on real macOS and Windows machines shook out platform bugs. v0.4.0 rolls all of that up under its own version number — still Linux-first, now genuinely at home on three platforms — and adds the hardening pass that came out of it.

## Highlights

- **macOS and Windows, field-tested** — every fix below was earned on real machines, not emulators: Docker discovery without a terminal's PATH (login-shell adoption on macOS, well-known install locations and Docker Desktop's named pipe on Windows), menus that open under WKWebView, external-tool buttons that speak each platform's language, and no console-window flashing on Windows.
- **The Windows storage saga, solved properly** — Windows bind mounts are root-owned and ignore chmod, so PHP inside the container could never write `storage/`. Mast now wires `SUPERVISOR_PHP_USER` through the compose file itself (the only place Sail actually reads it), bakes it in at bootstrap, and Diagnose repairs existing projects the same way — verified by re-probing as the user PHP really runs as, not by trusting file metadata.
- **Repairs live in Diagnose** — no more scattered Fix buttons on the card: everything is consolidated under Diagnose, and the button grows an amber hint icon when there is something worth clicking. Failed operations contribute their fixes too ("From the last failed operation").
- **Three new doctors** — app reachability (host TCP on both address families, then in-container curl), `APP_URL`/published-port mismatch, and storage writability probed by actually writing a file as the container's effective PHP user.
- **Port conflicts name names** — the preflight tells you which project is squatting the port and offers a targeted fix on the holder, with platform-aware hints for squatters outside Mast.
- **Elevation on every platform** — pkexec on Linux, osascript on macOS, and a real UAC prompt on Windows for hosts/CA repairs — with the result verified by re-reading the system state, because exit codes lie across elevation boundaries.
- **Bootstrap honors the installer** — a project born on `:8000` keeps it: `APP_PORT` follows `APP_URL` instead of rewriting the URL onto collision-prone `:80`.
- **Whole-project Rebuild** — one button (and `mast rebuild`) recreates the stack with `--build --remove-orphans` for the day a git pull changes the compose config underneath a running project.
- **The test suite runs everywhere** — macOS and Windows CI now execute the full workspace test suite on every commit, not just a type-check. The suites learned to tell a Windows-containers daemon from a Linux one, to skip instead of panic, and to survive 8.3 short paths, verbatim prefixes, and sequential ephemeral ports. The platform architecture — where each platform concern lives and the eight field-earned rules — is written down in ADR-0006.
- **Polish** — a transparent icon everywhere it has contrast (the Windows light taskbar keeps its tile), theme-aware tray icons, slim theme-aware scrollbars on macOS and Windows, a wider single-project view, and long git-branch chips that ellipsize instead of clipping.

## Binaries

Every platform, built by CI from this tag:

- **Linux x86_64** — `.deb`, `.rpm`, AppImage, and a CLI tarball (`mast` + `mast-daemon`)
- **macOS** — `.dmg` and CLI tarball for Apple Silicon (`aarch64`) and Intel (`x64`). Unsigned: the first launch needs System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway — the README walks through it.
- **Windows x64** — NSIS installer and a CLI zip. Unsigned: SmartScreen will warn on first run. Projects live on plain local paths (not OneDrive); WSL2-resident projects are a future feature.

name: Mast v0.3.0
body:
The Sail-friction release.

## Highlights

- **Trusted local HTTPS** — serve any project at `https://myapp.test` through one shared local Caddy proxy, with a certificate your browser trusts from an authority that never leaves your machine. The two one-time system steps (hosts entry, CA trust) are previewed Fix buttons — or fully manual, with everything copyable.
- **Browser trust, finished properly** — on Linux, Chromium-family browsers (Chrome, Vivaldi, Brave, Edge) read the NSS store, not the system store. Mast now detects that gap, and when `certutil` is missing, one Fix installs the NSS tools with your package manager and adds the certificate in the same run.
- **sail share, debuggable** — QR code, an exact preview of every `SAIL_SHARE_*` setting before the tunnel starts, automatic dashboard port pick, stale Vite hot-file detection, and orphan-tunnel cleanup.
- **PHP & Node switching + runtime view** — one verified operation per switch, and the PHP chip now shows live ini limits and loaded extensions with edit-and-rebuild buttons.
- **Application log viewer** — `storage/logs/laravel.log` parsed: stack traces grouped, level filters, clear-in-place.
- **Smarter service chips** — open Mailpit/Meilisearch/MinIO dashboards on their real ports; copy database credentials and a ready-made connection URL.
- **Commands with a working directory** — drive a sibling repo's dev server from the same project card.
- **Fix buttons on failures** — fourteen failure signatures explain what went wrong and, where possible, fix it in one previewed click.
- **A wider diagnostics net** — identity collisions, compose project-name pinning, DB credential and volume-version doctors, Xdebug ladder, env lint pack, MailHog→Mailpit migration, and more.
- **Bootstrap reliability** — the port probe now sees IPv6-only squatters before Docker trips over them; a moved `APP_PORT` drags a pinned `APP_URL` along so the Browser button never goes stale; and a container left half-started (running but detached from its network) is detected and recreated in one click.
- **Fresh-project doctors** — a reachable database that was never migrated (the "everything looks fine but every page 500s" trap) gets an Error finding with a one-click `artisan migrate`; a stale `APP_URL` port gets a previewed `.env` fix.
- **Per-project diagnostics** — a Diagnose button on every project card runs the checks scoped to that project's findings and fixes (`mast diagnose <project>` on the CLI), so the one project you care about isn't buried in the full report.
- **Cross-platform pass** — macOS-aware advice and elevation everywhere; macOS and Windows type-checked in CI on every commit.

## Binaries

Every platform, built by CI from this tag:

- **Linux x86_64** — `.deb`, `.rpm`, AppImage, and a CLI tarball (`mast` + `mast-daemon`)
- **macOS** — `.dmg` and CLI tarball for Apple Silicon (`aarch64`) and Intel (`x64`). Unsigned: right-click → Open on first launch.
- **Windows x64** — NSIS installer and a CLI zip. Full experience since the 2026-08-24 re-cuts: live container observation over Docker Desktop's named pipe, sail projects driven through `docker compose` (the sail wrapper is a bash script Windows cannot run), and the external-tool buttons speak Windows. Unsigned: SmartScreen will warn on first run.

## Re-cut history

The assets on this tag have been rebuilt in place as field-testing on real macOS and Windows machines shook out platform bugs — same links, reinstall to update:

- **Packaged-app PATH** — the dmg/exe find the docker CLI without a terminal's PATH (login-shell adoption on macOS, well-known install locations everywhere), and a missing Docker Desktop reads as instructions instead of a raw spawn error.
- **macOS menus** — App/Workspace/View open under WKWebView.
- **Windows, wired for real** — named-pipe observation, sail via `docker compose`, working Browser/Files/Editor/Terminal buttons, no console-window flashing, `\\?\` verbatim paths stripped (the "mount denied" fix), and app/tray icons that survive a light theme.
- **Orphan recovery** — containers left behind by an older compose config are marked on their chips, stoppable/removable individually, swept by whole-project Stop, and reaped by the new **Rebuild** button (`mast rebuild` on the CLI): the one-click recovery when a git pull changed the compose config underneath a running project.
- **New Fix buttons** — stale network endpoints (with a full leftover-container sweep), missing `vendor/` (containerized composer install), and missing `node_modules` (in-container install) are recognized failure signatures with one-click repairs.

name: Mast v0.2.0
body:
Two features since v0.1.0, both aimed at the same gap: Mast could say what was running, but nothing about what it was doing, or what it was costing.

## Log captures

A live log stream is bound to one container and ends when that container does — which is exactly when its output becomes worth reading. Recreating a container starts a fresh log and discards the old one, so by the time you know you wanted it, it is gone.

Mast now keeps the last minute of a container's output whenever it goes down:

- Before Mast stops, restarts or rebuilds it — taken before the command runs, because a rebuild removes the container.
- When it exits or turns unhealthy on its own, including while Mast was closed.
- When a workspace start gives up waiting for it to become ready.
- On demand, from the service menu.

Captures are written to disk, so they survive both the container being replaced and Mast being restarted. Values that look like secrets in your `.env` are removed before one is stored.

## Resource usage

Live CPU and memory per service, rolled up to project, workspace and a status-bar total, plus a Resources tab that ranks every running service so the answer to "what do I stop" is the top row.

CPU is reported in **cores**, not a percentage — Docker's percentage is a share of every core at once, so `800%` is a real reading on an eight-core box and no progress bar can express it. Memory is the working set, with reclaimable page cache excluded, as `docker stats` reports it. Where a container has a real memory limit, the bar shows how close it is to being OOM-killed; where it has none, the same ratio is simply its share of the machine.

Sampling only runs while the Mast window is visible. Measuring the machine costs CPU, and a minimised Mast should not be part of the problem it reports on.

## Also

- An **About Mast** dialog under the App menu, showing the running version, the resolved Docker endpoint, and which window currently has control.
- Fixed the frontend not being rebuilt during `cargo tauri build`, which could quietly ship a stale UI.

## Install

Linux x86_64. See the README for per-format instructions.

| Format | File |
| --- | --- |
| Debian / Ubuntu | `Mast_0.2.0_amd64.deb` |
| Fedora / RHEL | `Mast-0.2.0-1.x86_64.rpm` |
| Portable | `Mast_0.2.0_amd64.AppImage` |
